title: TikTok Return Models & Exchanges API Solution Guide
content:
# **Aftersales Transactions Overview** Returns/refunds, cancellations, & exchanges are post-sales (after-sales) actions that can be initiated by either buyers or sellers. TikTok Shop provides API scopes for sellers to programatically handle these cases: * **Cancel API**: Supports buyer-initiated cancellation requests and seller-initiated order cancellations. * **Return API**: Supports buyer-initiated refund or return-and-refund requests. **Cancel Order** Orders can be canceled at the buyer’s request or directly by the seller. Each canceled order includes the cancel reason, status, creation time, and seller processing time. In the US and UK, sellers can also partially cancel orders when items are out of stock. **Return Order** Return orders occur when a buyer requests a return or refund only for one or more items after delivery. Each return order includes the return/refund reason, status, request time, seller processing time, and refund amount. **This document will focus on Return transactions**, nuanced return label models, and give guidance on developing end-to-end solutions using the TikTok Shop open APIs based on the different return models. -- For a more **generalized** overview of all TikTok Shop Aftersales workflows, please see our documentation below: * [Return, refund, and cancel API overview](https://partner.tiktokshop.com/docv2/page/return-refund-and-cancel-api-overview) * [Return reasons](https://partner.tiktokshop.com/docv2/page/return-reasons) * [Refund reasons](https://partner.tiktokshop.com/docv2/page/refund-reasons) * [Cancel reasons](https://partner.tiktokshop.com/docv2/page/cancel-reasons) # **Aftersales Stages** Before diving into the detailed API sequence, it's important to understand the **stages** of an aftersales/return record in TikTok Shop. TikTok Shops measures the seller's actions in these different return stages, to ensure the buyer communications/experience meets our SLAs/policies. **Note**: These measured **stages** are *different* from the granular return **status** that are exposed in the API/webhooks | **Stage** | **What Happens** | **Seller Action** | **SLA / Deadline** | **Outcome / Notes** | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | **1st Review Stage:**
Return Request | Buyer submits a return request. TikTok now auto-approves **95%** of requests based on product category. Once approved, TikTok generates the official **RMA_ID** for the seller/ISV to capture the return and related line items. | For ~5% of requests that still require review, the seller must **approve or reject** the **request** via API or Seller Center.
| **24 hours** from request submission | If no decision is made within 24 hours, TikTok will **auto-approve** the request and generate the return shipping label. Some requests may require review due to restricted categories or suspicious buyer return activity. | | **2nd Review Stage:**
Return Decision | After the returned package is received and inspected, the seller reviews the refund decision. | Seller must **approve or reject the return,** based on their item inspection SOP or automated rules. | **4 business days** after return package's tracking shows `DELIVERED` | If no decision is made within 4 business days , TikTok will **auto-approve** the return, and the buyer will be refunded the money associated with their original payment. | For all return transactions, TikTok Shop API/webhooks expose the necessary return status updates, and delivery signals that enable sellers to indentify what action they need to perform next within the return lifecycle. # **Return Actions by Status** During the lifecycle of a return, there are specific actions buyers or sellers are allowed to perform, based on the forward `order_id` status, as well as what the `return_id` status. The following table illustrates when a "Return" can be **initiated** based on the current order status. | | **Initiator** | **`UNPAID` ** | **`ON_HOLD`** | **`AWAITING_SHIPMENT`** | **`AWAITING_COLLECTION`** | **`IN_TRANSIT`** | **`DELIVERED`** | **`Completed`** | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | **Return**

Once the seller selects which return label model is required for their systems, they can build a holistic returns management integration with TikTok's open APIs for either of these return models. | **Return Model** | **Description** | | --- | --- | | ### **4PL Model:**
**TikTok Return Labels**
| TikTok is responsible for generating the return shipping label, using our own TikTok carrier accounts.

***Note****: The TikTok Shop definition for 3PL labels means this is a 3rd party logistics* ***label,*** *not necessarily coming from a 3rd party logistics fulfillment provider. 3PL labels can come from a seller's own UPS/USPS/Fedex accounts, or these labels could be generated by a return platform such as:* ***Loop Returns****,* ***Happy Returns*** *etc.*

*This ability to generate and upload a 3rd party return shipping label is* ***commonly referred to as V2 Returns*** *within the TikTok ecosystem.*

Offer partial refund | | | | | **PATH D** | **[15.D]** OMS RMA status = Same sku / multiple quantity has different conditions.
| **WMS** | RMA contains multiple quantities of the exact same sku (SKU:A x 2 QTY) Warehouse associated inspects the package/items and finds that:
QTY 1 is in good condition
QTY 2 is completely damaged/or missing altogether. | | **PATH D** | **[16.D] Instruct TTS app** `OFFER_PARTIAL_REFUND`
| **OMS** | Based on warehouse items grading results, 1 QTY should be refunded, 1 QTY should be rejected due to the damage. However, as previously stated, TikTok shop platform has a known gap where we do not allow different refund decisions if there are multiple quantities of the same sku_id. To solve for this platform behavior, OMS must perform calculations to trigger a partial refund amount for each qty/line, which is meant to equate to the total amount the buyer should receive. Example:
Buyer orders SKU:A x 2 QTY. Each item original cost paid = $10.00
QTY 1 is received in "good/sellable" condition
QTY 2 is damaged or missing.
-
The seller wants to **approve** QTY 1 and **reject** QTY 2, so that the buyer is only refunded **$10.00** out of the original $20.00 amount paid for both lines. However, the TTS platform/API does not allow different decisions for the same SKU (known platform behavior/limitation).

The seller can use the Review Aftersales API and use the `OFFER_PARTIAL_REFUND` enumeration for both lines. However, OMS logic **must** calculate the amount using the formula
(Total amount to refund buyer) / (total # of return_line_item_ids)
Example from above:
$10.00 (total amount to refund buyer) / (2 return_lines) = $5.00
The `OFFER_PARTIAL_REFUND` amount will be `5.00` for **both** lines of the same SKU, to ensure the buyer will receive $10.00 for their refund amount.

The `OFFER_PARTIAL_REFUND` can also be used as an appeasment mechanism. For example
**IF**: the buyer was only expected to send back SKU A, QTY 1, but the item was slightly damaged, noticeably worn, package slightly damaged etc
**THEN**: the seller can make a decision to `OFFER_PARTIAL_REFUND` for that single return_line_item_id, and TikTok will refund that buyer the amount specified by the seller. | # **3PL Model: External Return Labels** ***Also known as: V2 Returns*** The **most common** use-case for the 3PL label model is when sellers want to leverage their existing DTC return platforms with TikTok return activity. Oftentimes, sellers' DTC process will leverage **return platforms** that are responsible for **generating a shipping label** for the buyers, and **orchestrating the data flows** and for operational functions between the return platform and their own DTC/OMS/WMS layers. By leveraging these **existing** return platform workflows for TikTok Shop returns, sellers can **alleviate engineering efforts and costs**. And maintain a **consistent** end-to-end process between their DTC and TikTok Shop returns. Also, some sellers have customized attributes/barcodes rendered on the return shipping label through these return platforms. These label attributes are part of their warehouse SOPs for scanning and identifying return packages once received at their warehouse facilities. ### Return platforms that have partnered with TikTok to build the 3PL label/QR code model: * Loop Returns * Happy Returns * Amazon MCF * Redo Returns * Narvar (scoping in progress) At a high-level, these existing return platform integrations follow this model outlined below 1. Capture the new return/RMA details 2. Generate a 3rd party return shipping label (3PL, off TikTok's platform) 3. Upload that the 3rd party return back to TikTok to render/email to the buyer 4. Submit the return/RMA details to their return warehouse's systems (WMS/DB) 5. Buyers use the seller's 3PL label to send the return package to the seller's return warehouse location 6. Warehouse operations identify the return package, inspect and grade the items 7. Based on the warehouse grading, send return status to an OMS layer for refund decision to return platform/app. 8. Return Platform app to send TikTok the decision to either APPROVE or REJECT the return refund to the buyer. However, sellers **do not** have to leverage these existing return platform integrations. They are also able to **develop their own 3PL label model**. **** This essentially allows the seller to perform the exact steps the return platforms are managing outlined above, but the seller **use their own label** and upload directly between their systems and TikTok's API. ![Image](https://p16-arcosite-sg.ibyteimg.com/tos-alisg-i-k9wyc2ijk0-sg/6f1e289079bf429b9306a3087f211caf~tplv-k9wyc2ijk0-image.image) > ### **3PL Model Prerequisites Checklist** There are multiple prerequisite configurations required for each sellers' shops. Sellers must have the following checklist completed **before** they are able to test the label generation & label upload flow back to the TikTok app buyer view. | **Checklist Tasks** | **Owner** | **Comments** | | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Define which **`seller_id`**(s) needs 3PL label functionality | Seller/TTS | Share sandbox and production **`seller_id`**(s) with TikTok solutions POC for backend configuration | - [ ] | | Define which **`app_key`** will be managing return APIs | Seller/TTS | Share **`app_key`** with TikTok solutions POC for backend configuration | - [ ] | | Define which exact carrier return methods to offer buyers
| Seller/TTS
| TikTok needs to configure the **`seller_id`** to only display the seller's expected return methods in buyer UX journey. Carrier return methods vary between carriers: **`USPS`**, **`UPS`**, **`Fedex`**. And each carrier has variations in return methods for shipping labels vs dropoff QR codes. | - [ ] | | Request API access for [Upload Shipping Document API](https://partner.tiktokshop.com/docv2/page/upload-shipping-document-and-tracking-info-202405) | Seller/TTS | TTS solutions POC must whitelist your **`app_key`** to access this API scope. | - [ ] | | Request API access for new batch returns API/Webhooks

| Seller | Share the TikTok **`user_id`** with TikTok solutions POC to flag as "test" user, which can access test shop products to perform order creation, and return submission to validate the 3PL label upload is properly rendered in the TikTok app.

However, as previously stated, TikTok shop platform has a known gap where we do not allow different refund decisions if there are multiple quantities of the same sku_id. To solve for this platform behavior, OMS must perform calculations to trigger a partial refund amount for each qty/line, which is meant to equate to the total amount the buyer should receive. Example:
Buyer orders SKU:A x 2 QTY. Each item original cost paid = $10.00
QTY 1 is received in "good/sellable" condition
QTY 2 is damaged or missing.
-
The seller wants to **approve** QTY 1 and **reject** QTY 2, so that the buyer is only refunded **$10.00** out of the original $20.00 amount paid for both lines. However, the TTS platform/API does not allow different decisions for the same SKU (known platform behavior/limitation).

The seller can use the Review Aftersales API and use the `OFFER_PARTIAL_REFUND` enumeration for both lines. However, OMS logic **must** calculate the amount using the formula
(Total amount to refund buyer) / (total # of return_line_item_ids)
Example from above:
$10.00 (total amount to refund buyer) / (2 return_lines) = $5.00
The `OFFER_PARTIAL_REFUND` amount will be `5.00` for **both** lines of the same SKU, to ensure the buyer will receive $10.00 for their refund amount.

What happens if I receive the return package, and my warehouse inspects the item(s) to find them either damaged or missing? What processes do I have to dispute with the buyer and TikTok? **Answer:** As a seller, you can submit an arbitration process to dispute the damaged/missing items you were expecting to receive for this exchange. **Question 2:** Is this a breaking change? **Answer:** No. This is an additive response field. Existing integrations will continue to work **Question 3**: Does my app need a new authorization scope? **Answer:** Apps that already call Returns & Order scopes do not need new authorization.
